The morning arrives slowly in this small kitchen where light falls through the east window like a quiet letter no one has opened yet. I make tea not because I need energy but because the steam gives my hands something gentle to hold while the world wakes up around me. Outside a bicycle leans against a brick wall and a cat watches traffic with the serious patience of animals who understand streets better than people do.

I think about letters I never sent and songs I never learned and promises I made to myself in January when the year seemed full of clean possible roads. Some of those roads led nowhere except back to this same chair by the same window and that is not failure but simply proof that living asks for revision more than speed. I open a notebook to record small things that mattered today, the sound of rain on tin roof, the price of bread, a joke from a stranger at the market, and the way my sister laughs at her own story before she even finishes it.

Later I will walk to the library and return three books I borrowed last winter and pretend I have read every page. The librarian will smile because she knows exactly what I am doing and that kindness feels like forgiveness without any lecture. For now I sit here listening to kettle and watching light move across floor as if time itself were a cat crossing a room softly.
